x: In the A.A.A. two miles at White City on July 19th, he once again put up a very fast time of 13.56 only to be beaten by the holder, Hindmar by the very small margin of two seconds.

It was Churcher—Hindmar over again, only more so. Jim kept the Frenchman from getting inside, but when he concluded the Frenchman had had enough Maggi proved him wrong, got in front and stayed there to set up a new French record in two minutes faster than his previous best.

However he persevered and won through, and demonstrated his strength of character and his will to succeed to such an extent that he was again placed (2nd and 3rd) in the AAA "2' and "7' ; Hindmar of Sweden, winning both Championships.

Harry Churcher set a thrilling pace in the 2 miles walk, but was pipped by Hindmar of Sweden. Then Willie Nankeville set us roaring by making the pace in the 1 mile final, and he eventually finished 3rd to Garay (Hungary) and Slykhuis (Holland) in the record time of 4 mins. 10.6 secs.
